status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) section 71119 requires states to establish Medicaid community engagement requirements for certain adults, going beyond the Mandate's call for state options by making the requirement mandatory. CMS published an interim final rule on 2026-06-03 (effective 2026-07-31; correction 2026-06-29): adults in the expansion group must show 80 hours a month of work, community service, a work program or education, or equivalent income, subject to exclusions and verification, with state compliance required by 2027-01-01. A coalition of state attorneys general and two governors sued on 2026-06-29 (Massachusetts et al. v. Oz, D. Mass.), and on 2026-07-29 the court denied a preliminary injunction without prejudice, leaving the rule in effect while expedited merits briefing proceeds. The same law adds six-month eligibility renewals for the expansion adult group (section 71107, for renewals on or after 2027-01-01, with CMS guidance in a 2026-03-06 State Medicaid Director Letter) and cost sharing for certain expansion adults (section 71120, effective 2028-10-01 per CMS); no time limit or lifetime cap on benefits appears in the CMS summaries of the law.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed; Title VII, Subtitle B, Chapter 1 includes sections 71107 (eligibility redeterminations), 71119 (community engagement requirement) and 71120 (cost sharing for expansion adults).
CMS issues State Medicaid Director Letter #26-001 on implementing six-month eligibility renewals for the adult expansion group under section 71107, for renewals scheduled on or after 2027-01-01.
CMS publishes the interim final rule implementing the community engagement requirement (CMS-2454-IFC, 91 FR 33348).
Federal Register publishes a correction to the interim final rule.

A coalition of 24 attorneys general (23 states and the District of Columbia) and the governors of Kentucky and Pennsylvania sues over the CMS interim final rule (Massachusetts et al. v. Oz), alleging it unlawfully narrows the medically frail exemption, violates the Administrative Procedure Act and coerces states.

Judge Richard Stearns (D. Mass.) denies the states' motion for a preliminary injunction without prejudice, finding no showing of irreparable harm and noting 90 percent federal funding of state system costs; the rule stays in effect, with expedited merits briefing planned before 2027-01-01.
Interim final rule takes effect; the comment period closes the same day.
